Current work

Inside enterprise
technology governance.

I support an enterprise SaaS and third-party software portfolio: the intake, evaluation, decision, and follow-through behind the software a large organization runs on.

Intake & Evaluation

What comes in, and whether it holds up
  • Review renewals, net-new software requests, proofs of concept, and technology intake requests.
  • Evaluate each request across business value, ownership, security, identity access, governance, contingency, vendor, and Product Catalog requirements.
  • Escalate unclear cases with structured options so leaders can reach consistent decisions.
Every request is framed the same way before review: business need, named owner, value case, deadline. A request that cannot name its owner does not move forward until it can.

Governance Controls & Trackers

The operational control layer of the portfolio
  • Manage and improve SaaS governance trackers and operational control views used in recurring reviews.
  • Identify missing Product Catalog IDs and coordinate remediation across requesters, engagement owners, business units, Product Catalog, IAM, CyberArk, SailPoint, and procurement.
  • Track contingencies, ownership, follow-ups, aging requests, and approval dependencies.
  • Guide requesters through Product Catalog onboarding and other post-approval requirements.
Each record carries a catalog status (confirmed, missing, needs validation, onboarding in progress, or not applicable), an owner, and a next step, so the portfolio can be reviewed at a glance instead of reconstructed by hand.

Executive Decision Support

Raw input in, decision-ready information out
  • Convert raw information from SharePoint, intake forms, requesters, engagement owners, senior directors, trackers, and working sessions into decision-ready information.
  • Write executive summaries and recommendations built on request IDs, software categories, risks, dependencies, outstanding actions, and governance findings.
  • Present data, recommendations, and unresolved questions to working councils and executive consulting teams.
The format is fixed: ask first, findings second, open questions named. Councils decide in the room because the reconciliation happened before it.

Reporting & Process Improvement

Visibility leaders can plan around
  • Produce leader-wise data pulls across the enterprise.
  • Build Excel control trackers with PivotTables, filtered operational views, conditional formatting, and status logic; support Power BI reporting and dashboard validation.
  • Improve recurring processes by defining status categories, ownership models, review cadences, guidance documents, and repeatable workflows.
  • Work across security, IAM, procurement, business, technology, and leadership teams.
Totals are validated before anything reaches a leader, and recurring exceptions feed back into status definitions and guidance instead of being fixed one record at a time.

Project DossierAMBER · AI Governance

Project Amber: AI Governance Intake & Risk Triage

Prepared by Sumanth Cholleti Document type Project brief Basis Original methods, sample data only

AMBER started with a pattern I kept meeting in real intake queues. An AI tool would surface months after adoption, usually during a renewal or a catalog reconciliation, already holding company data, provisioned with local accounts outside SSO, no MFA enforcement, no entitlement review, and a vendor agreement nobody had read for the model training clause. On the status tracker, the same tool showed green. The scoring said approved; the evidence said otherwise. That gap between the dashboard and the ground truth is what I could not unsee.

So I built the triage I wished existed. AMBER takes a proposed AI tool and scores what actually creates exposure: data classification, from public to regulated; model autonomy and whether a human stays in the loop; identity posture across SSO, SCIM provisioning, and privileged access; and the vendor terms that decide whether your prompts become someone else’s training data. It returns a risk tier, a decision path, and the compensating controls required before approval, structured on the NIST AI RMF functions: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage. My vision: governance engineered like a product, rigorous enough for security, fast enough that the business never routes around it.

The problem
Shadow AI discovered after adoption, scored green while running outside identity, access, and vendor controls.
The insight
Exposure is knowable at intake, if data class, autonomy, access posture, and training terms are scored before approval instead of audited after incidents.
What it proves
I can design the control system, not just operate inside one.

Project DossierNorth Star · Product Management

Project North Star: Executive Decision Brief Builder

Prepared by Sumanth Cholleti Document type Project brief Basis Original methods, sample data only

North Star came from the mechanics of my daily work. A single enterprise request might live in five places at once: an intake form, a SharePoint list, a tracker with ownership fields that contradicted the form, a stakeholder position buried in an email thread, and a dependency on an IAM review that nobody had logged. Then a council is asked to decide, on aging information, with the request already weeks old. I kept rebuilding the same missing structure by hand, reconciling sources, chasing owners, re-deriving the options. Eventually the pattern was undeniable: the decision was never the hard part. The assembly was.

North Star is that assembly, productized. It ingests the fragmented record and produces a one-page executive brief: the ask stated cleanly, findings reconciled across sources, options scored with explicit trade-offs, risks and dependencies named with owners, and a single recommendation that a named human stands behind. Change any input and the brief rebuilds, so the decision stays traceable from raw intake to final call. My vision: product management practiced as decision infrastructure, where no leader ever has to decide on top of fragments again.

The problem
Councils deciding complex requests from contradictory records scattered across forms, trackers, and inboxes.
The insight
Decision quality is an assembly problem. Force ask, evidence, options, and risk onto one page, with owners attached, and the right call usually makes itself.
What it proves
I already run the core motion of a product manager: discovery, reconciliation, prioritization, and a defensible recommendation.
